signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5810, supported by an average 1W performance of +0.854% across G10 pairs for AUD against CHF's -0.464%, creating a 1.319% leader-to-laggard G10 spread. RBA policy rate at 4.60% versus SNB at 0.00% yields a +460bp rate differential favoring AUD, reinforcing structural carry demand over Swiss franc defensive flows. US 5Y yields stand at 5.06% with a 20D rise of +54bp driven entirely by real yields (+54bp real, +0bp breakeven, FRED, as of Oct 02), illustrating a broader high-real-yield environment that penalizes zero-yielding CHF. Cross-asset volatility highlights this divergence as the MOVE index reaches the 96th percentile of its trailing year while VIX sits at the 11th percentile (15.0), signaling fixed income policy repricing that favors yield-backed currencies. Technical positioning shows AUD/USD holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7036/0.7093, though the bilateral AUD strength continues to dominate CHF crosses. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF on yield differential expansion. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hold priced. Risk: Broad equity risk-off spike lifting VIX above 25 and driving defensive flows into CHF.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.27, anchored above its SMA20 at 156.64 and SMA50 at 157.79 while holding below the SMA200 at 158.50. Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% generates a +275bp policy rate differential, while OIS rates (SOFR 3.89% vs TONA 1.23%) confirm a +266bp CIP carry premium supporting the dollar. Options markets show institutional hedging with 25d Risk Reversals at -2.01 (Saxo, 1M tenor), indicating a strong put skew as traders pay up for JPY downside protection against intervention or hawkish BoJ shifts. USD/JPY 1M implied volatility sits at 8.4% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.9%, producing a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.4% that reflects thin options supply despite elevated spot levels. CFTC positioning registers JPY Leveraged Funds net short at -16,809 contracts (96th percentile of its 52-week range), leaving spec shorts vulnerable to policy headlines despite recent real wage gains backing BoJ normalization. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding above 156.64 moving average support. Catalyst: FOMC Minutes release at 18:00 UTC. Risk: BoJ policy shift or official intervention above 160.00 triggering a spec short squeeze.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Premium + Retail Long Extreme
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1257, positioned below its SMA20 (1.1426), SMA50 (1.1524), and SMA200 (1.1608) technical cluster. Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a +135bp policy rate differential favoring USD, backed by SOFR 3.89% vs €STR 2.44% (+145bp OIS carry premium). Options markets reflect elevated hedging demand with 1M implied volatility at 6.2% versus 30-day realized volatility at 4.1%, delivering a +2.0% Vol Risk Premium (Saxo, 1M tenor) alongside a -0.85 25d risk reversal put skew. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short -82,445 contracts (6th percentile of 52-week range, WoW -23,640), aligning with EUR Economic Sentiment Index at +10.9. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows 85% of retail traders long EUR/USD, creating an extreme retail long positioning that directly diverges from institutional spec shorts and reinforces downside trend continuation. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; institutional net shorts and negative carry outweigh retail contrarian positioning. Catalyst: ECB Monetary Policy Meeting Accounts at 11:30 UTC. Risk: Break above SMA20 at 1.1426 forcing leverage short covering.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT Short vs OIS Hold Bias
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4213, holding above its SMA20 (1.4063), SMA50 (1.3964), and SMA200 (1.3860) technical cluster. Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.25% provides a +175bp rate spread, corroborated by SOFR 3.89% vs CORRA 2.29% (+160bp OIS spread) favoring USD carry. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold CAD net short -72,519 contracts (long% 23.8%, WoW -23,396), reflecting heavy spec short accumulation even as CAD ESI prints at a strong positive +15.1 index score. Retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data is 96% short USD/CAD, establishing an extreme retail short bias that fades the institutional net long USD backdrop and price trend. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by rate differential and trend structure above 1.4063. Catalyst: BoC meeting 28 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Sharp crude oil rally above $95/bbl boosting CAD terms of trade.
